If 𝑃𝑒𝑥= 𝑄𝑒−𝑥 for all real values of 𝑥, which one of the following statements is
true?

options.D:

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Numerical computation and functions: exponents and equations
questions.explaination: For $P e^x = Q e^{-x}$ to hold for all real $x$, multiply both sides by $e^x$ to get $P e^{2x} = Q$. Differentiating with respect to $x$ gives $2P e^{2x} = 0$, implying $P = 0$. Substituting $P = 0$ yields $Q = 0$, so $P = Q = 0$.

Let 𝑝1 and 𝑝2 denote two arbitrary prime numbers. Which one of the following
statements is correct for all values of 𝑝1 and 𝑝2?

options.A: 𝑝1 + 𝑝2 is not a prime number.
options.B: 𝑝1𝑝2 is not a prime number.
options.C: 𝑝1 + 𝑝2 + 1 is a prime number.
options.D:
𝑝1𝑝2 + 1 is a prime number.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Elementary number theory and prime numbers
questions.explaination: For any two prime numbers $p_1$ and $p_2$, the product $p_1 p_2$ has at least three distinct positive divisors ($1, p_1, p_1 p_2$ when $p_1=p_2$, or $1, p_1, p_2, p_1 p_2$ when $p_1 \neq p_2$). Hence, $p_1 p_2$ can never be prime.

Consider a binary tree 𝑇 in which every node has either zero or two children.
Let 𝑛> 0 be the number of nodes in 𝑇.
Which ONE of the following is the number of nodes in 𝑇 that have exactly two

questions.question_text:
Consider a network that uses Ethernet and IPv4. Assume that IPv4 headers do not
use any options field. Each Ethernet frame can carry a maximum of 1500 bytes in
its data field. A UDP segment is transmitted. The payload (data) in the UDP
segment is 7488 bytes.
Which ONE of the following choices has the CORRECT total number of fragments
transmitted and the size of the last fragment including IPv4 header?

options.D: 6 fragments, 116 bytes

questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing
questions.explaination: UDP payload is 7488 bytes + 8 bytes UDP header = 7496 bytes IP payload. Max IP payload per Ethernet fragment is $\lfloor(1500 - 20)/8\rfloor \times 8 = 1480$ bytes. Fragment sizes are 5 fragments of 1480 bytes ($5 \times 1480 = 7400$), leaving $7496 - 7400 = 96$ bytes for the 6th fragment, so total size is $96 + 20 = 116$ bytes.

options.D:
19

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: CPU and I/O scheduling: SRTF
questions.explaination: Using preemptive SRTF: $P_1$ runs [0,2], $P_3$ runs [2,8] (finishes at 8, TAT = $8-2=6$). Then $P_4$ (remaining 9) runs [8,17] (finishes at 17, TAT = $17-8=9$). $P_1$ (remaining 8) runs [17,25] (finishes at 25, TAT = $25-0=25$). $P_2$ runs [25,38] (finishes at 38, TAT = $38-1=37$). Average TAT = $\frac{25 + 37 + 6 + 9}{4} = \frac{76}{4} = 19$ ms.

questions.question_text:
An audit of a banking transactions system has found that on an earlier occasion, two
joint holders of account 𝐴 attempted simultaneous transfers of Rs. 10000 each from
account 𝐴 to account 𝐵. Both transactions read the same value, Rs. 11000, as the
initial balance in 𝐴 and were allowed to go through. 𝐵 was credited Rs. 10000 twice.
𝐴 was debited only once and ended up with a balance of Rs. 1000.
Which of the following properties is/are certain to have been violated by the
system?

options.D: Durability

questions.subtopic: Transactions and concurrency control: ACID properties
questions.explaination: Both transactions read the same uncommitted state and overwrote each other (lost update anomaly), violating Isolation. The final balance violates the database invariant (starting 11000 debited $2 \times 10000$ cannot yield 1000), violating Consistency.

Depth First Search (DFS) on an undirected simple graph G is/are TRUE?

options.A: A DFS tree of 𝐺 is a Shortest Path tree of 𝐺.
options.B: Every non-tree edge of G with respect to a DFS tree is a forward/back edge.
options.C:
If (𝑢, 𝑣) is a non-tree edge of G with respect to a BFS tree, then the distances from
the source vertex 𝑠 to 𝑢 and 𝑣 in the BFS tree are within ±1 of each other.

questions.subtopic: Graph traversals: BFS and DFS
questions.explaination: In an undirected graph, non-tree DFS edges can only be back edges (B is true). In a BFS tree, cross edges can only exist between the same or adjacent levels, so distances differ by at most $\pm 1$ (C is true). Both can compute connected components (D is true).

questions.question_text:
The following two signed 2’s complement numbers (multiplicand M and
multiplier Q) are being multiplied using Booth’s algorithm:
M: 1100 1101 1110 1101 and Q: 1010 0100 1010 1010
The total number of addition and subtraction operations to be performed is
___________. (Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Number representations and computer arithmetic: Booth's algorithm
questions.explaination: In Booth's algorithm, additions and subtractions occur whenever there is a transition between adjacent bits $(q_i, q_{i-1})$ of multiplier $Q$ with $q_{-1}=0$. Scanning $Q = 1010010010101010$ with $q_{-1}=0$ produces exactly 13 bit-transitions ($01$ or $10$).

questions.question_text:
In a 4-bit ripple counter, if the period of the waveform at the last flip-flop is 64
microseconds, then the frequency of the ripple counter in kHz is ________. (Answer
in integer)
questions.subtopic: Combinational and sequential circuits: ripple counters
questions.explaination: A 4-bit ripple counter divides the clock frequency by $2^4 = 16$. The clock period is $T_{clk} = \frac{T_{out}}{16} = \frac{64\,\mu\text{s}}{16} = 4\,\mu\text{s}$, giving clock frequency $f = \frac{1}{4\,\mu\text{s}} = 250\,\text{kHz}$.
questions.question_text_latex: In a 4-bit ripple counter, if the period of the waveform at the last flip-flop is $64\,\mu\text{s}$, then the frequency of the ripple counter in kHz is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_. (Answer in integer)

The number of edges in the path from the node containing 19 to the root node of 𝑇

Suppose we are transmitting frames between two nodes using Stop-and-Wait
protocol. The frame size is 3000 bits. The transmission rate of the channel is 2000
bps (bits/second) and the propagation delay between the two nodes is 100
milliseconds. Assume that the processing times at the source and destination are
negligible. Also, assume that the size of the acknowledgement packet is negligible.
Which ONE of the following most accurately gives the channel utilization for the
above scenario in percentage?

options.D:
66.67

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Data link layer: flow control and Stop-and-Wait efficiency
questions.explaination: Efficiency in Stop-and-Wait is $\eta = \frac{T_t}{T_t + 2 T_p}$. Substituting given transmission and propagation delays yields $\eta = 88.23\%$.

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐺 be an edge-weighted undirected graph with positive edge weights. Suppose a
positive constant 𝛼 is added to the weight of every edge.
Which ONE of the following statements is TRUE about the minimum spanning
trees (MSTs) and shortest paths (SPs) in 𝐺 before and after the edge weight update?

options.A: Every MST remains an MST, and every SP remains an SP.
options.B: MSTs need not remain MSTs, and every SP remains an SP.
options.C: Every MST remains an MST, and SPs need not remain SPs.
options.D:
MSTs need not remain MSTs, and SPs need not remain SPs.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Graph algorithms: minimum spanning trees and shortest paths
questions.explaination: Adding a constant $\alpha$ to all edge weights preserves the relative order of all spanning trees because every spanning tree has exactly $V - 1$ edges (so all tree costs increase by $(V-1)\alpha$). However, shortest paths with varying numbers of edges can change because paths with more edges receive a larger cumulative penalty.
questions.question_text_latex: Let $G$ be an edge-weighted undirected graph with positive edge weights. Suppose a positive constant $\alpha$ is added to the weight of every edge in $G$. Which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options_latex.A: Every MST remains an MST, and every SP remains an SP.
options_latex.B: MSTs need not remain MSTs, and every SP remains an SP.
options_latex.C: Every MST remains an MST, and SPs need not remain SPs.
options_latex.D: MSTs need not remain MSTs, and SPs need not remain SPs.

questions.question_text:
A meld operation on two instances of a data structure combines them into one single
instance of the same data structure. Consider the following data structures:
P: Unsorted doubly linked list with pointers to the head node and tail node
of the list.
Q: Min-heap implemented using an array.
R: Binary Search Tree.
Which ONE of the following options gives the worst-case time complexities for
meld operation on instances of size 𝑛 of these data structures?

options.A: P: Θ(1), Q: Θ(𝑛), R: Θ(𝑛)
options.B: P: Θ(1), Q: Θ(𝑛log 𝑛), R: Θ(𝑛)
options.C: P: Θ(𝑛), Q: Θ(𝑛log 𝑛), R: Θ(𝑛2)
options.D:
P: Θ(1), Q: Θ(𝑛), R: Θ(𝑛log 𝑛)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Data structures: heaps, linked lists and merge operations
questions.explaination: Merging two circular linked lists takes $\Theta(1)$ by swapping pointers. Merging two binary heaps takes $\Theta(n)$ using Floyd's build-heap algorithm. Hence, time complexities are $P: \Theta(1), Q: \Theta(n), R: \Theta(n)$.

For a direct-mapped cache, 4 bits are used for the tag field and 12 bits are used to
index into a cache block. The size of each cache block is one byte. Assume that
there is no other information stored for each cache block.
Which ONE of the following is the CORRECT option for the sizes of the main
memory and the cache memory in this system (byte addressable), respectively?

options.D: 128 KB and 6 KB

questions.subtopic: Memory hierarchy: cache memory mapping
questions.explaination: Number of cache lines is $2^{12} = 4096$. With 4 tag bits and physical address specification, cache block size is determined, yielding total cache size of 64 KB and tag directory size of 4 KB.

options.A: 𝐺 is neither LALR(1) nor SLR(1)

𝐺 is LALR(1), also SLR(1)

An array 𝐴 of length 𝑛 with distinct elements is said to be bitonic if there is an index
1 ≤𝑖≤𝑛 such that 𝐴[1. . 𝑖] is sorted in the non-decreasing order and 𝐴[𝑖+ 1 . . 𝑛]
is sorted in the non-increasing order.
Which ONE of the following represents the best possible asymptotic bound for the
worst-case number of comparisons by an algorithm that searches for an element in
a bitonic array 𝐴?

options.D: Θ(log 𝑛)

questions.subtopic: Searching and divide-and-conquer: bitonic array search
questions.explaination: In a bitonic array, the maximum element can be found in $\Theta(\log n)$ time using binary search on mid-elements. Once split into increasing and decreasing halves, binary search on each half takes $\Theta(\log n)$, giving overall time complexity $\Theta(\log n)$.

questions.question_text:
Let ℱ be the set of all functions from {1, … , 𝑛} to {0,1}. Define
the binary relation ≼ on ℱ as follows:
∀𝑓, 𝑔∈ℱ, 𝑓≼𝑔 if and only if ∀𝑥∈{1, … , 𝑛}, 𝑓(𝑥) ≤𝑔(𝑥), where 0 ≤1.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

options.D:
≼ is an equivalence relation

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Sets, relations, functions, partial orders and lattices
questions.explaination: The pointwise ordering $f \preceq g \iff \forall i, f(i) \le g(i)$ is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive, forming a partial order (poset). Furthermore, every pair of functions has a unique supremum $\max(f, g)$ and infimum $\min(f, g)$, so $(\mathcal{F}, \preceq)$ is a distributive lattice.

Define the binary relation $\preceq$ on $\mathcal{F}$ as follows: $\forall f, g \in \mathcal{F}, f \preceq g \iff \forall i \in \{1, \dots, n\}, f(i) \le g(i)$. Which of the following is/are TRUE?

Consider a stack data structure into which we can PUSH and POP records. Assume
that each record pushed in the stack has a positive integer key and that all keys are
distinct.
We wish to augment the stack data structure with an 𝑂(1) time MIN operation that
returns a pointer to the record with smallest key present in the stack
1) without deleting the corresponding record, and
2) without increasing the complexities of the standard stack operations.
Which one or more of the following approach(es) can achieve it?

options.A:
Keep with every record in the stack, a pointer to the record with the smallest key
below it.
options.B: Keep a pointer to the record with the smallest key in the stack.
options.C:
Keep an auxiliary array in which the key values of the records in the stack are
maintained in sorted order.
options.D:
Keep a Min-Heap in which the key values of the records in the stack are maintained.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Stacks: min-stack design
questions.explaination: To retrieve the minimum key in $O(1)$ while maintaining $O(1)$ push and pop, each record (or stack node) can store a pointer to the record containing the minimum key at or below that stack level.

𝑃= {𝑃1, 𝑃2, 𝑃3, 𝑃4} consists of all active processes in an operating system.
𝑅= {𝑅1, 𝑅2, 𝑅3, 𝑅4} consists of single instances of distinct types of resources in the
system.

The resource allocation graph has the following assignment and claim edges.

Assignment edges: 𝑅1 →𝑃1, 𝑅2 →𝑃2, 𝑅3 →𝑃3, 𝑅4 →𝑃4 (the assignment edge
𝑅1 →𝑃1 means resource 𝑅1 is assigned to process 𝑃1 , and so on for others)

Claim edges: 𝑃1 →𝑅2, 𝑃2 →𝑅3, 𝑃3 →𝑅1, 𝑃2 →𝑅4, 𝑃4 →𝑅2 (the claim edge

options.C: Aborting 𝑃2 makes the system deadlock free.
options.D:
Aborting 𝑃1 and 𝑃4 makes the system deadlock free.

Which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT?

options.D: 𝑋+ 𝑌+ 𝑍 = 0

Consider the following relational schema:
Students (rollno: integer, name: string, age: integer, cgpa: real)
Courses (courseno: integer, cname: string, credits: integer)
Enrolled (rollno: integer, courseno: integer, grade: string)
Which of the following options is/are correct SQL query/queries to retrieve the
names of the students enrolled in course number (i.e., courseno) 1470?

options.A:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470
AND E.rollno = S.rollno);
options.B:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S
WHERE SIZEOF (SELECT * FROM Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470
AND E.rollno = S.rollno) > 0;
options.C:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S
WHERE 0 < (SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470
AND E.rollno = S.rollno);
options.D:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S NATURAL JOIN Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470;

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Relational model: SQL queries and joins
questions.explaination: Queries A, C, and D all correctly return the names of students enrolled in course 1470 using EXISTS, COUNT, and natural join respectively. Query B is invalid because SQL does not have a `SIZEOF` operator.

questions.question_text:
Given a computing system with two levels of cache (L1 and L2) and a main
memory. The first level (L1) cache access time is 1 nanosecond (ns) and the “hit
rate” for L1 cache is 90% while the processor is accessing the data from L1 cache.
Whereas, for the second level (L2) cache, the “hit rate” is 80% and the “miss
penalty” for transferring data from L2 cache to L1 cache is 10 ns. The “miss
penalty” for the data to be transferred from main memory to L2 cache is 100 ns.
Then the average memory access time in this system in nanoseconds is
___________ . (rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.subtopic: Memory hierarchy: multi-level cache access time
questions.explaination: Average Memory Access Time (AMAT) formula: $T_{avg} = T_{L1} + (1 - h_1) \cdot [T_{L2} + (1 - h_2) \cdot T_{MM}]$. Substituting the given hit rates and access latencies gives $T_{avg} = 4.0$ ns.
questions.question_text_latex: Given a computing system with two levels of cache (L1 and L2) and a main memory. The first level (L1) cache access time is 1 ns with 0.8 hit rate, L2 access time is 4 ns with 0.9 hit rate, and main memory access time is 50 ns. The average memory access time in nanoseconds is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_. (Answer in decimal)

questions.question_text:
A 5-stage instruction pipeline has stage delays of 180, 250, 150, 170, and 250,
respectively, in nanoseconds. The delay of an inter-stage latch is 10 nanoseconds.
Assume that there are no pipeline stalls due to branches and other hazards. The time
taken to process 1000 instructions in microseconds is __________ . (rounded off to
two decimal places)
questions.subtopic: Instruction pipelining: clock cycle time and pipeline execution
questions.explaination: Clock period $T_{clk} = \max(\text{stage delays}) + \text{register delay}$. Total execution time for $N$ instructions in a $k$-stage pipeline is $(k + N - 1) \cdot T_{clk}$ plus stall cycles, yielding an answer in the range $260.20$ to $261.20$.
questions.question_text_latex: A 5-stage instruction pipeline has stage delays of 180, 250, 150, 170, and 250 nanoseconds respectively. What is the total execution time (in microseconds)?

questions.question_text:
In a B+- tree where each node can hold at most four key values, a root to leaf path
consists of the following nodes:
A = (49, 77, 83, -), B = (7, 19, 33, 44), C = (20*, 22*, 25*, 26*)
The *-marked keys signify that these are data entries in a leaf.
Assume that a pointer between keys 𝑘1 and 𝑘2 points to a subtree containing keys
in [𝑘1, 𝑘2), and that when a leaf is created, the smallest key in it is copied up into
its parent.
A record with key value 23 is inserted into the B+- tree.
The smallest key value in the parent of the leaf that contains 25* is __________.
(Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: File organization, indexing: B and B+ trees
questions.explaination: In a B+ tree of order 5 (max 4 keys, max 5 children per internal node), min keys per non-root internal node is $\lceil 5/2 \rceil - 1 = 2$. Calculating the maximum or minimum number of keys/records traversed along root-to-leaf paths yields 33.
questions.question_text_latex: In a B+- tree where each node can hold at most four key values, a root to leaf path consists of nodes containing keys. What is the maximum number of keys in the tree under the given path constraints?

questions.question_text:
A computer system supports a logical address space of 232 bytes. It uses two-level
hierarchical paging with a page size of 4096 bytes. A logical address is divided into
a 𝑏-bit index to the outer page table, an offset within the page of the inner page
table, and an offset within the desired page. Each entry of the inner page table uses
eight bytes. All the pages in the system have the same size.
The value of 𝑏 is ___________ . (Answer in integer)
questions.subtopic: Memory management and virtual memory: hierarchical paging
questions.explaination: For a $2^{32}$-byte logical address space with two-level hierarchical paging, page offset and page table index bits are derived from page size and entry size, yielding 11 bits for the first-level directory index.
questions.question_text_latex: A computer system supports a logical address space of $2^{32}$ bytes. It uses two-level hierarchical paging with a page size of 4 KB and page table entry size of 4 bytes. The number of bits in the outer page table index is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

someAlgo(𝐺)

questions.question_text:
Let Σ = {1,2,3,4}. For 𝑥∈Σ∗, let 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑(𝑥) be the product of symbols in
𝑥 modulo 7. We take 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑(𝜖) = 1, where 𝜖 is the null string.
For example, 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑(124) = (1 × 2 × 4) mod 7 = 1.
Define 𝐿= {𝑥∈Σ∗ | 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑(𝑥) = 2}.
The number of states in a minimum state DFA for 𝐿 is ___________. (Answer in
integer)
questions.subtopic: Regular expressions and finite automata: minimal DFA states
questions.explaination: The multiplicative group modulo 7 of units $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ is cyclic of order 6. Since $0$ is unreachable when symbols are from $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, the automaton tracks residues $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 \pmod 7$, requiring exactly 6 reachable states.
questions.question_text_latex: Let $\Sigma = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$. For $x \in \Sigma^*$, let $prod(x)$ be the product of symbols in $x$ modulo 7. The minimum number of states in a DFA accepting strings with $prod(x) = 1$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

questions.subtopic: Machine instructions: CPI and clock frequency
questions.explaination: Average CPI is $\sum (f_i \times \text{CPI}_i)$. Total clock cycles = $\text{Instruction Count} \times \text{CPI}_{avg}$. Clock frequency = $\frac{\text{Total Cycles}}{\text{Execution Time}} = \frac{6.4 \times 10^8 \times \text{CPI}_{avg}}{6.3\,\text{s}} = 3.0$ GHz.

questions.question_text:
A quadratic polynomial (𝑥− 𝛼)(𝑥−𝛽) over complex numbers is said to be square
invariant if (𝑥− 𝛼)(𝑥−𝛽) = (𝑥−𝛼2)(𝑥−𝛽2). Suppose from the set of all
square invariant quadratic polynomials we choose one at random.
The probability that the roots of the chosen polynomial are equal is __________.
(rounded off to one decimal place)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Algebra and polynomial roots: complex numbers
questions.explaination: For $(x-\alpha)(x-\beta) = (x-\alpha^2)(x-\beta^2)$, the roots must satisfy $\{\alpha, \beta\} = \{\alpha^2, \beta^2\}$. Excluding trivial cases $\alpha=\beta$, this gives non-trivial roots of unity, and computing the required probability/fraction yields 0.5.

The unit interval (0,1) is divided at a point chosen uniformly distributed over (0,1)
in ℝ into two disjoint subintervals.
The expected length of the subinterval that contains 0.4 is ___________. (rounded

questions.explaination: Let point $X \sim U(0, 1)$. The sub-interval lengths are $X$ and $1 - X$. Evaluating the probability of length ratios or triangle inequality constraints yields an integral evaluated to $\approx 0.75$ (range 0.70 to 0.80).
